guardianfootball.title: Rayan Cherki magic denies Napoli but Manchester City’s struggles continue
guardianfootball.description: For reasons best known to those eyeing the pound signs, Manchester City gave a debut to a special rust-coloured kit in front of a nonplussed crowd. It was of a piece with their performance for most of a familiarly frustrating night that at least concluded with a shot of energy, the home side belatedly shaking off their torpor and ending the prospect of a triumphant return to the Etihad for Kevin De Bruyne. Despite the relief sparked by a fine equaliser by Rayan Cherki, who was rewarded for an insistent but hitherto fruitless evening’s endeavours when his angled shot flashed past Vanja Milinkovic-Savic, it was hard to see this as anything but a perfect snapshot of their autumn difficulties.…

guardianfootball.description: Arsenal’s sky-high standards are slipping. For the second time in four days, Mikel Arteta’s side found themselves a goal up at half-time and apparently coasting toward victory, only for their opponents to rouse themselves and earn a deserved draw. After Newcastle on Saturday , this time it was an impressive Borussia Dortmund who became only the second side to take points off Arsenal in their past 15 group stage games in this competition. It could have been worse had an offside flag not ruled out Jobe ­Bellingham’s goal after Max Beier equalised a thunderbolt from Viktor Gyökeres. But the much-maligned Sweden striker was guilty of a glaring miss late on as Arsenal laid siege to Dortmund’s…

guardianfootball.title: Gul takes pain for buoyant Galatasaray to condemn Aston Villa to Champions League loss
guardianfootball.description: This was Aston Villa’s third trip to Istanbul in the calendar year but, this time, they departed with different emotions. Unlike on the banks of the Bosphorus at Besiktas Park in May, the scene of their unforgettable Europa League triumph , or at Fenerbahce in January, they came away with a bloody nose. Galatasaray’s match-winner, Deniz Gul, finished with similar, the substitute requiring a bandage after bravely taking a boot to the face from Nicolas Jackson as the hosts rippled the net on 77 minutes. It was the game’s first effort on target, Galatasaray maintaining their commanding form on home soil to extend Villa’s winless run to six matches in all competitions. On the outside, this is…

Despite the Football Association ruling the Frenchman’s early sending-off in Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool was “wrongful dismissal”, Manchester United remain furious at the decision, and at Pro Ref, the elite officials’ organisation. Continue reading...

guardianfootball.description: Senegal won January’s final 1-0 after walking off Result was overturned in March as 3-0 win for Morocco Senegal have been reinstated as the champions of Africa, and their controversial 1-0 victory against Morocco confirmed in the record books, after the scandal over January’s Africa Cup of Nations final was resolved in a Swiss courtroom. The court of arbitration for sport (Cas) ruled that a decision to award the 2025 Afcon title to Morocco on appeal should be set aside. Senegal celebrated with a social media post proclaiming the team to have won the title twice: first on the field and then at Cas. Morocco, who are due to co-host the World Cup in 2030, declared their intention to “pursue…

Having been restored to the starting lineup at the Riverside, the Championship’s leading scorer claimed his 14th league goal of the season to re-establish his side’s lead in the second half after Joseph Opoku’s driven finish had cancelled out Myles…

guardianfootball.description: Playmaker in best form since moving to Anfield ‘I am really enjoying playing under Iraola’ Florian Wirtz has credited Andoni Iraola with helping him recapture the form that made him one of the most coveted players in Europe when he joined Liverpool in a deal worth up to £116m in 2025. The Germany international believes he is in the best form of his Liverpool career, having had a difficult debut season under Arne Slot and also struggled in the early weeks of Iraola’s reign. Wirtz scored an exquisite improvised goal in the 4-0 defeat of Manchester United on Sunday when he also created 10 chances from open play. Continue reading...

guardianfootball.title: Crystal Palace docked three WSL points for extra substitution against Everton
guardianfootball.description: Too many substitutes used during win in opening game They drop place to 13th but no extra points for Everton Crystal Palace have been deducted three points in the Women’s Super League after they made substitutions in four separate windows during their 1-0 victory over Everton in September. Palace admitted breaching the competition’s rules and an independent tribunal ordered the points deduction, but no points will be awarded to Everton. It means Palace drop from 12th to 13th, below Birmingham City on goal difference. The match will not be replayed. Continue reading...

pitchfork.title: Fly 1111
pitchfork.description: The Texas singer-songwriter’s debut channels a cool-girl-next-door vibe and a twangy alt-pop sound. At her best, she sounds wise beyond her years, with a knack for hooks and a literary imagination.

pitchfork.title: American Bully XL
pitchfork.description: On its second album, the Texas quartet runs classic country influences through blasts of distortion, pairing its noisy palette with newly confessional lyrics.

pitchfork.title: Thanatos
pitchfork.description: Bradford Cox’s first solo album in 15 years is a haunted, autumnal meditation on all forms of decay: bodily, spiritual, political, and sonic.

pitchfork.title: Demoed EP
pitchfork.description: MJ Lenderman, Circuit des Yeux, Flock of Dimes, and more lend their voices to stripped-down versions of songs from this year’s Punching the Clown on a new EP that continues the remarkable transformation of Lambchop.

pitchfork.title: Khudgarzi
pitchfork.description: The Brooklyn and Delhi-based singer-songwriter tells stories of strange and solitary women cast out by society: murderers, sex workers, and schemers determined to secure their freedom by any means.

pitchfork.title: Glitter
pitchfork.description: Each Sunday, Pitchfork takes an in-depth look at a significant album from the past, and any record not in our archives is eligible. Today, we revisit the superstar’s infamous eighth album and film soundtrack, an effervescent blend of retro synth-pop, aughties hip-hop, and piano balladry with legendary baggage.

pitchfork.title: Reveal (25th Anniversary Edition)
pitchfork.description: The rock band’s sunny synth-pop pivot remains an undersung gem. On a new reissue, it also feels like a touchstone for the sound of indie-pop in the 21st century.

pitchfork.title: Live at the Barbican
pitchfork.description: Two years after her long-awaited solo debut, the Pixes/Breeders/Amps singer-songwriter returns with an opulent concert album that pushes her abundant personality to the fore.

quietus.title: Rafael Toral Details New Album, ‘Long Ways’
quietus.description: It's out on Drag City in February Photo by Vera Marmelo Rafael Toral will start 2027 with the release of a new album, titled Long Ways. Made up of three extended pieces, the album breaks free from the orchestral arrangements of 2025 album Traveling Light and 2024's Spectral Evolution, according to a press release. It was largely built from a process of improvisation. Commenting on the album, Toral said: "Long Ways is a development forward from the previous two albums, but condensing everything into playing guitar. It’s all about sound, or better, the stillness of presence. The music itself here is less important than the sound of playing. What I’m after is an abstraction, the sound of…

quietus.title: TIDAL to Delete and Ban Fully AI-Generated Music
quietus.description: Over the past 90 days, 43% of all tracks distributed to the platform have been detected as wholly AI-generated, the streaming service revealed TIDAL has confirmed plans to delete and ban music that has been fully created using artificial intellignece tools. From 9 December, any wholly AI-generated track will be rejected and removed from the platform, while all songs that have already been uploaded and identified as entirely produced using AI will also be deleted from the streaming service. Announcing the change, TIDAL revealed that 43% of all tracks distributed to the platform have been detected as wholly AI-generated over the last 90 days. These tracks have been labelled as such in order…

quietus.title: Supersonic Reveals First Acts Playing 2027 Lineup
quietus.description: Shudder To Think and La Tène are among those lined up to play the Birmingham event next year Shudder To Think, photo by Seth Olenick Supersonic has shared the first lineup announcement for its 2027 edition next spring. Veteran Washington D.C. punk and post-hardcore band Shudder To Think, who've newly reformed, will head up the lineup, while French-Swiss tQ favourites La Tène are also lined up to play the Birmingham festival. The lineup announcement also takes in experimental black metal group Genital Shame; hardcore duo Iron Lung; noise rock trio Rhododendron; hardcore band Nekra; Rocket Recordings affiliates Pharaoh Overlord; Jerusalem In My Heart's Radwan Ghazi Moumneh performing with…

quietus.title: Posthumous D’Angelo Song Released on Grand Theft Auto VI Soundtrack
quietus.description: The late artist approved use of the song in the long-anticipated game before his death last year A previously unreleased song by D'Angelo has been released as a standalone single after it appeared in the soundtrack for the much-anticipated new game Grand Theft Auto VI. 'Kamikazi' features among the list of tracks that can be heard on the Gilles Peterson-hosted Worldwide FM within the game. "Michael approved this track in its current form in November of 2024 to be released as part of Grand Theft Auto VI,” the late artist's brother, Luther Archer Jr, said in a statement. "He was a tremendous admirer of Rockstar Games and a past collaborator of theirs. He was enthusiastic (to say the least)…

quietus.title: Rockfort! French Music for November, Reviewed by David McKenna
quietus.description: In his final French dispatch of 2026, David McKenna examines the pioneering legacy of the Saravah label as it turns 60 under bittersweet circumstances, and presents 10 essential new records from folk to hip hop Elizabeth Vogler and donkey friends by Albane Barrau 2026 marks 60 years since the founding of the Saravah label, but the festivities have been bittersweet since it has also been 10 years since the death of its founder Pierre Barouh. Not only that but earlier this year Areski, an essential part of the Saravah family and Brigitte Fontaine’s partner, died at the age of 86. What remains, though, is a still-vital legacy that is being celebrated through three reissues: Fontaine and…

quietus.title: Philip Golub – Loop 8/9
quietus.description: Philip Golub Loop 8/9 Stripping music back to a bare minimum, the Brooklyn composer explores the tiny transformations that take place when human hands repeat the same musical activity again and again and again Loop 8/9 by Phillip Golub Over the last few years Brooklyn keyboardist, composer and bandleader Philip Golub has emerged as a major figure straddling the worlds of jazz, experimental and contemporary practice, in part, by refusing to compartmentalise his various interests within sacrosanct projects. Earlier this year he released Partisan Ship (Berthold), a wild album that reinforced his contributions to an evolving jazz trend incorporating microtonality or different tuning systems,…

quietus.title: Overmono Share Five Tracks Made for Grand Theft Auto VI Soundtrack
quietus.description: The UK duo shared score duties with Justice for the much-anticipated game Overmono have shared five original tracks that they made for the widely anticipated new game Grand Theft Auto VI. Last week, it emerged that the UK duo had provided the additional score for the game, with Justice handling the bulk of the original soundtrack. Overmono were behind the pause music composition, which has become an early favourite of those playing the game, while they also made songs for other challenges and parts of the map. The duo's previously released songs 'Even Angels Ghost' and 'Good Lies' also feature on one of the game's radio stations, the PinkPantheress and The Dare-hosted Stockyard FM. Their…

quietus.title: Nikola Balberčáková on New Album and PAF Olomouc Appearance
quietus.description: Irina Shtreis talks to Nikola Balberčáková about her troubling AV piece r/ForeverAlone and the new work she will present in Olomouc this December Social media narratives may not be the easiest material to work with when creating convincing artwork. It can be hard to sift through layers of superfluous information. Genuine personal stories often get tangled up with attempts at creative writing. Despite potential pitfalls, Prague-based Slovakian artist Nikola Balberčáková delved into online forums in order to produce a critically-acclaimed audiovisual work called r/ForeverAlone. The 2024 project drew inspiration from the eponymous digital community on Reddit. The content on the titular…

aquariumdrunkard.title: The Lagniappe Sessions :: Shane Butler
aquariumdrunkard.description: Shane Butler's first solo record, Heavy Debt , is due next month, and for this Lagniappe Session he's pulled together three songs that have been rattling around for a long time. Fugazi's "I'm So Tired," a song he first encountered as a kid watching skate videos, Shoes' homemade pop and a 1979 Soft Boys' nugget.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Miles Davis: Copenhagen Live 1969
aquariumdrunkard.description: Miles Davis’ 1969 live ensemble existed in a parallel timeline alongside his studio work - greasing his audience for a future for which they were wholly unprepared. A new 2LP set, Copenhagen Live 1969 , captures the band at its peak, stress-testing then-unreleased Bitches Brew material, tearing it down and reassembling it into some of the most far-out, formless music of Miles’ career.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Frank Black :: The Aquarium Drunkard Interview
aquariumdrunkard.description: In 2025, Pixies leader Frank Black took to the road to celebrate the 30th anniversary of his 1994 sophomore LP Teenager of the Year with the same cast of players who recorded the original album. A sprawling double album, it's held together with the same kind of ramshackle logic that makes The Beatles' The White Album or The Clash's London Calling work. Recently, Aquarium Drunkard caught up with Black to discuss revisiting the album. Along the way, he revealed details about a Pixies record in the works, UFOs, the paranormal, and explained his vision of a future rock & roll cult where artists like The Feelies are elevated to the status of saints.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Fine :: Jazz Dreams
aquariumdrunkard.description: For all the creativity Copenhagen’s avant-pop scene can offer, a lot of it had started to hang on its own clichés. Who knew it could be recharged by a blasé attitude and a good old dose of harmonic complexity? Fine’s Jazz Dreams is full of the kind of drowsy virtuosity that once again justifies the hype over that scene's prolific output; it's as if you were inhabiting the fantasies of a conservatory student who fell asleep in counterpoint class.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Tía Rosa :: Thirteen Automatic Dreams
aquariumdrunkard.description: Via Mexico City, Thirteen Automatic Dreams is the thrillingly comfy new record by Tía Rosa. Here is some minimalist kosmische with a Latin pop sensibility, a bridge between the noisy regularity of Neu! and the sugared melancholy of balada romántica. It all plays like a lost soundtrack to the Nevada desert of the Nocilla Trilogy , where shoes hang from a lonely poplar, or like Stereolab is being collectively hallucinated from one of those little Durango towns where Jodorowsky liked to film his deranged acid westerns.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Sunday Mourners :: A-Rhythm Absolute
aquariumdrunkard.description: Skirting the edges of canonical post-punk, the debut record by four piece Sunday Mourners is a gripping, youthful art-rock explosion. There are distinct flashes tapping into Chairs Missing -era jagged melodicism here, VU at their most intractable jamming there (the twelve minute "Darling" a prime example). Above all, A-Rhythm Absolute is a downright lively listen, hitting all of the spirited guitar-centric benchmarks to make the listener a reinvigorated believer in the state of such a modern landscape.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Happy Thanksgiving :: Doug Sahm And Friends – Austin, TX 1972
aquariumdrunkard.description: Tradition runs rampant around Thanksgiving: generations of old recipes, football, Alice’s Restaurant, and, of course, a parade of balloons shutting down NYC. What else do you need? If you thought you were covered in the Thanksgiving tradition department, we did too…until a few years ago, when someone blew the dust off a long lost tape — Doug Sahm’s Thanksgiving Jam.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Yr Knives :: Begin Yr Singing
aquariumdrunkard.description: On a recent episode of Vish Khanna's Kreative Kontrol podcast, Douglas McCombs explained that music his his primary social activity. This explains the bassist's extensive resume, which includes Tortoise, Brokeback, BASIC, Black Duck, Eleventh Dream Day, and The Sea and Cake. With Chicago's Yr Knives, he adds yet another group to the mix. On the group's debut, Begin Yr Singing , he joins drummer Quin Kirchner and guitarists Brian J Sulpizio (Health & Beauty) and Andrew Trim for a wild ride that hypnotically blends progressive rock, free jazz, krautrock, and desert blues. If one were scrambling for a genre, you could select "post-rock," but could equally apply the even less loved term "jazz…

mubi.title: A World in Parts
mubi.description: The Journey (Peter Watkins, 1987). At Radio Canada, preparations are underway for Ronald Reagan’s 1985 summit with Canadian prime minister Brian Mulroney. Filmmaker Peter Watkins and his crew have been allowed into meetings where the broadcasters plan their coverage down to the second. Everyone must synchronize their watches: A discrepancy of 40 seconds, one participant warns, could throw off the day’s work. A shot requested at 17:02 might be missed if recorded 30 seconds later. “One thing is certain: there can’t be anything unexpected tonight,” another member of the team declares. Security officials will provide the presidential route, street by street, allowing the text to be prepared…

His filmography moves between intricate narratives rooted in political and crime thrillers, and deeply intimate and socially driven dramas. mubi.title: The Last Emperor: A Conversation with Jeremy Thomas

A list of filmmakers whose work makes up Thomas’s production portfolio reads like a who’s who of maverick visionaries, each of them fiercely loyal to the last: Nicolas Roeg and David Cronenberg; Takeshi Kitano and Jonathan Glazer; Nagisa Ōshima and Wim Wenders; Jerzy Skolimowski and Bernardo Bertolucci, whose The Last Emperor (1987) won Thomas the Academy Award for…
